slides.0.title: Western Languedoc: Corbières, Minervois, Fitou
slides.0.subtitle: The big Aude appellations and their crus
slides.1.title: Corbières: the biggest AOC
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Scale
slides.1.highlights.0.content: About 13,500 ha across 87 communes in the Aude; AOC in 1985 (wein.plus); soils are slate, sandstone, limestone and marl
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Mostly red
slides.1.highlights.1.content: About 90% is red, blended from at least two of Carignan, Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre; whites use Grenache Blanc, Macabeu, Roussanne, Marsanne and Vermentino (wein.plus)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Subzones
slides.1.highlights.2.content: wein.plus lists 11 subzones (Boutenac, Durban, Fontfroide, Lagrasse and others). Sources differ on a Carignan cap ("up to 50%" or none stated), so it is not tested
slides.1.content: Corbières is a varied microcosm that no single style sums up.
slides.2.title: Boutenac and La Livinière
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Corbières-Boutenac
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Its own AOC in 2005 (Gérard Bertrand and wein.plus agree); Carignan-centred; Bertrand lists about 240 ha and 10 communes
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Minervois-La Livinière
slides.2.highlights.1.content: In the foothills of the Montagne Noire and Syrah-led; sources give 1998 or 1999 and conflicting areas, so we do not compare them
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The new names
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Registered in 2024 in the EU Official Journal as AOP La Livinière and AOP Boutenac (Gérard Bertrand; a producer's text, to be checked against official sources)
slides.2.content: Both sit at the top village tier, with different leads: Carignan versus Syrah.
slides.3.title: Minervois rules
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Proportions
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Carignan and Cinsault capped at 40% combined; Syrah, Mourvèdre, Grenache and Lledoner Pelut at least 60%, with Syrah plus Mourvèdre at least 20% (Winewisdom)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Climate
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Cooler than Corbières thanks to air from the Montagne Noire, with some Atlantic influence in the west (Winewisdom)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Soils
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Limestone, red shales, schist and clay marls
slides.3.content: Both in the Aude, but Minervois is cooler and Syrah-leaning.
slides.4.title: Fitou and neighbours
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Two separate blocks
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Fitou was recognised by decree on 28 April 1948: about 2,500 ha over nine communes, with a coastal Maritime zone (clay-limestone, rarely above 150 m) and an inland Hautes-Corbières zone (mostly schist, 100–400 m) about 20 km apart (Wine With Seth)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Rules
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Carignan at least 40%; Carignan plus Grenache at least 60% with at least 20% of each; no variety above 80%; at least two varieties; at least 9 months' ageing; max 54 hL/ha (Wine With Seth)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: The Atlantic edge
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Cabardès and Malepère on the western edge take Atlantic influence and mix Bordeaux and southern varieties (general description; details not tested)
slides.4.content: Fitou's two separate blocks and its Carignan minimum are classic exam points.
